finding.headline: At 44, the 401(k) limit for 2027 is $25,500, and the IRA limit is $7,500.
details: For 2027, the annual 401(k) contribution limit rises to $25,500, up from $24,500 for 2026.
The IRA contribution limit stays at $7,500 for 2027, so saving through both accounts has room to grow.
You plan to retire at 65. Sign up for Medicare at 65 even if you keep working, or your coverage may be delayed and cost more.

finding.headline: About 18% of your pay goes to tax now, and about 10% of withdrawals in retirement.
details: Now, total tax on your $74,000 pay is $13,075, which leaves $60,925 after tax.
In retirement, the plan draws on taxable savings first, then your 401(k), and Roth accounts last. Almost all your savings sit in pre-tax accounts, so most withdrawals will be taxed.
This is a rough guide, not tax advice. A tax professional can check the details for you.

finding.headline: You can count on $26,900 a year: $23,800 for basics and $3,100 for the rest.
details: Your basics cost about $23,800 a year.
Your spending goal of $55,000 a year lasts in 0 of 100 scenarios.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.

Until you retire you save about $6,725 a year: $4,000 into a 401(k) or IRA, $2,000 from your employer's match, $725 of take-home pay left after your spending, which the plan assumes you save. If that is wrong, change 'Yearly saving' in your answers.
Pay stays at today's level until you retire, with no raises. This is fixed: raises are not certain, so the plan does not count on them. If your pay changes, change it in your answers.
Your spending in retirement leaves out the mortgage. The payments left after you retire, until 2054, are counted as a cost of their own.
Social Security uses the figure you gave, read as the benefit at 67. It starts at 67: $29,000 a year.
If you retire before Medicare starts at 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until then (an assumption). Other health costs follow CMS figures by age.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving comes off taxable pay. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 93. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.
